targetTexts.2: “If only my grief could be weighed and placed with my calamity on the scales.
targetTexts.3: For then it would outweigh the sand of the seas—no wonder my words have been rash.
targetTexts.4: For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
targetTexts.5: Does a wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
targetTexts.6: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg?
targetTexts.7: My soul refuses to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.
targetTexts.8: If only my request were granted and God would fulfill my hope:
targetTexts.9: that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
targetTexts.10: It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
targetTexts.11: What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
targetTexts.12: Is my strength like that of stone, or my flesh made of bronze?
targetTexts.13: Is there any help within me now that success is driven from me?
targetTexts.14: A despairing man should have the kindness of his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
targetTexts.15: But my brothers are as faithless as wadis, as seasonal streams that overflow,
targetTexts.16: darkened because of the ice and the inflow of melting snow,
targetTexts.17: but ceasing in the dry season and vanishing from their channels in the heat.
targetTexts.18: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.
targetTexts.19: The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope to find it.
targetTexts.20: They are confounded because they had hoped; their arrival brings disappointment.
targetTexts.21: For now you are of no help; you see terror, and you are afraid.
targetTexts.22: Have I ever said, ‘Give me something; offer me a bribe from your wealth;
targetTexts.23: deliver me from the hand of the enemy; redeem me from the grasp of the ruthless’?
targetTexts.24: Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.
targetTexts.25: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
targetTexts.26: Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?
targetTexts.27: You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
targetTexts.28: But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
targetTexts.29: Reconsider; do not be unjust. Reconsider, for my righteousness is at stake.
targetTexts.30: Is there iniquity on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern malice?
